subject: indian_polity
question: Who is considered the chief architect of the Constitution of India?

explanation.simple: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and is known as the Father/Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution.

methods.name: Constitutional History
steps: Drafting Committee headed by Dr. Ambedkar.

explanation.exam_tip: Drafting committee had 7 members with Dr. Ambedkar as Chairman.

subject: indian_polity
question: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?

explanation.simple: The Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day) and came into full effect on 26th January 1950 (Republic Day).

methods.name: Dates
steps: 26 November is National Law Day / Constitution Day.

explanation.exam_tip: Adopted = 26 Nov 1949; Commenced = 26 Jan 1950.

subject: indian_polity
question: Which of the following words was NOT present in the original Preamble in 1950?

explanation.simple: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
steps: Added by 42nd Amendment: Socialist, Secular, Integrity.
explanation.exam_tip: 42nd Amendment (1976) added three words: Socialist, Secular, Integrity.

subject: indian_polity
question: Who moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946?

explanation.simple: Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the Objectives Resolution, which later formed the philosophical basis of the Preamble.

methods.name: Preamble Origin
steps: Objectives Resolution evolved into the Preamble.

explanation.exam_tip: Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946.

subject: indian_polity
question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble IS an integral part of the Constitution?

explanation.simple: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the SC overruled Berubari Union (1960) and held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution and can be amended without altering the basic structure.

methods.name: Landmark Rulings
steps: Kesavananda Bharati establishes Preamble as part of Constitution.

explanation.exam_tip: Largest ever constitutional bench (13 judges) in Kesavananda Bharati case.

subject: indian_polity
question: How many times has the Preamble of the Indian Constitution been amended so far?

explanation.simple: The Preamble has been amended only once till date, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
explanation.exam_tip: Preamble has been amended only once in history.

subject: indian_polity
question: Who was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly?

explanation.simple: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary/interim President on 9 Dec 1946. On 11 Dec 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as permanent President.
explanation.exam_tip: Temporary: Sachchidananda Sinha; Permanent: Rajendra Prasad.

subject: indian_polity
question: The idea of 'Liberty, Equality and Fraternity' in the Preamble was inspired by which revolution?

explanation.simple: Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity were the central motto of the French Revolution (1789-1799). Justice (Social, Economic, Political) was borrowed from the Russian Revolution (1917).
explanation.exam_tip: French Revolution: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. Russian Revolution: Justice.

subject: indian_polity
question: Which feature of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland?

explanation.simple: DPSP (Part IV) and the nomination of members to Rajya Sabha were borrowed from Ireland (Irish Constitution).
explanation.exam_tip: Ireland: DPSP, nomination of Rajya Sabha members, Presidential election method.

subject: indian_polity
question: The concept of 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution was propounded in which year?

explanation.simple: The Basic Structure doctrine was introduced by the 13-judge bench in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala on 24 April 1973.
explanation.exam_tip: Judgment was delivered on 24 April 1973.

subject: indian_polity
question: What is the correct sequence of words in the Preamble as per the Constitution?

explanation.simple: The opening declaration reads: 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC' (abbreviated SO-SO-SE-DE-RE).
explanation.exam_tip: Memorize sequence: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.

subject: indian_polity
question: Who was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly?

explanation.simple: Sir Benegal Narsing Rau (B. N. Rau) was the Constitutional Advisor who prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.
steps: Constitutional Advisor: Sir B. N. Rau.

methods.name: Historical Post
steps: B. N. Rau prepared the primary draft.

explanation.exam_tip: Do not confuse Drafting Chairman (Ambedkar) with Constitutional Advisor (B. N. Rau).

subject: indian_polity
question: Which schedule was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951?

explanation.simple: The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment in 1951 to protect land reform laws from judicial review.
explanation.exam_tip: Original Constitution had 8 schedules; currently there are 12.

subject: indian_polity
question: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to complete the Constitution of India?

explanation.simple: The Constituent Assembly sat for exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days across 11 sessions.
steps: Dec 9, 1946 to Nov 26, 1949 = 2 yrs, 11 mos, 18 days.
explanation.exam_tip: Frequently asked in state and railway exams.

subject: indian_polity
question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in the Indian Constitution was adopted from which country?

explanation.simple: Judicial Review, Fundamental Rights, Independent Judiciary, and Impeachment of President were borrowed from the US Constitution.
steps: USA: Judicial Review, Preamble, Fundamental Rights.
explanation.exam_tip: UK has parliamentary sovereignty; USA has judicial review.

subject: indian_polity
question: Under which Article of the Constitution can Parliament amend the Constitution?

explanation.simple: Article 368 in Part XX empowers Parliament to amend the Constitution by way of addition, variation, or repeal, subject to the basic structure doctrine.
explanation.exam_tip: Borrowed from South Africa.

subject: indian_polity
question: In which case did the Supreme Court explicitly rule that the 9th Schedule is open to judicial review for laws violating the basic structure enacted after 24 April 1973?

options.text: I. R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)

explanation.simple: In I. R. Coelho (2007), a 9-judge bench ruled that laws placed in the 9th Schedule after 24 April 1973 are subject to judicial review if they violate fundamental rights forming part of the basic structure.
explanation.exam_tip: Coelho judgment eliminated total immunity of 9th Schedule.

subject: indian_polity
question: Which of the following bodies was NOT created by the Constitution (i.e. is Non-Constitutional)?

explanation.simple: Finance Commission (Art 280), Election Commission (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315) are constitutional bodies. NITI Aayog was established by an executive resolution on 1 January 2015 and is non-constitutional and extra-statutory.
explanation.exam_tip: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission via executive resolution.

subject: indian_polity
question: What is the legal status of the Preamble in Indian courts?

options.text: It is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced directly in court
It is justiciable and enforceable like Fundamental Rights
It overrides express provisions of Articles
It cannot be used as an interpretive aid

explanation.simple: The Preamble is non-justiciable (its provisions are not directly enforceable in courts of law), but it acts as a key to unravel the minds of the makers and aids in constitutional interpretation.
steps: Cannot be enforced in court directly.
explanation.exam_tip: Preamble is non-justiciable; it is neither a source of power nor a prohibition.

subject: indian_polity
question: Who among the following was the calligrapher of the original handwritten Constitution of India?

explanation.simple: Prem Behari Narain Raizada handwrote the original Constitution in flowing italic style. Nandalal Bose and artists from Santiniketan decorated and illuminated each page.

methods.name: Art & Calligraphy
steps: Raizada wrote the English text by hand.

explanation.exam_tip: Raizada was the calligrapher; Nandalal Bose was the artist.
